triggerReasons.message: High-risk or gate/security wording selects high-assurance intent hardening.
High-assurance work requires an independent intent-collision result.
Ambiguity, user impact, behavior change, or multi-deliverable intent makes intent collision diagnostically required.
Bug, regression, security/auth/session, benchmark, or explicit behavior-change work should have red evidence.
Broad or absolute scope wording should have scope clarification before future enforcement.

acceptanceBindings.note: Truncation removal: real DEV-gate rejections differing past the former 200-character cut digest distinctly, and the counter consequence (maxGateFailureCount stays 1) is asserted, not just the hash.
Path rule narrowed to token-start absolute paths: slash-bearing identifiers and repo-relative files stay distinct while machine-specific roots still collapse.
Digit rule narrowed to standalone numbers: identifier-embedded ordinals stay distinct while free-standing counters still collapse.

Two-direction matrix is the guard on the inverse risk: must-still-collapse cases must still reach count 2 and trip assessBreaker, and each rule reverted individually must fail a named subset so a regression localizes.

diagnosticGaps.message: Scope ambiguity is triggered but no scope contract or explicit shrinkage decision is configured.

note: Four bindings, one per checklist item. The acceptance claim is satisfied only when BOTH directions hold: substantively distinct rejections get distinct keys (AB-001 through AB-003) and incidentally-different retries still share a key and still trip the breaker (AB-004).
